continue.resumed: Pick up where you left off

board.title: Meet the board
board.intro: Six parts you will use lab after lab. Drag the board to turn it; pick a part to light it up and see which labs use it.
board.model: 3D model of the PULSAR C6: the ESP32-C6 chip with its ceramic antenna, one USB-C port, BOOT and RST buttons, the RGB LED, the microSD slot, the Qwiic connector and two rows of header pins. Drag to turn it.
board.fallback: Every part is described in the cards.

usb.title: USB-C port
usb.text: One port flashes the board and carries the serial monitor: the C6 speaks USB itself, no bridge chip.

buttons.title: BOOT and RST
buttons.text: RST restarts your program. BOOT is GPIO 9: a free push button once the board runs.

rgb.title: RGB LED
rgb.text: One WS2812B on GPIO 8: 16 million colours from a single data pin.

module.title: ESP32-C6 chip
module.text: A 160 MHz RISC-V core, a low-power core and 4 MB of flash inside the chip. No PSRAM.

antenna.title: Chip antenna
antenna.text: Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5 and Thread/Zigbee leave from this small ceramic part: keep it clear of metal.

headers.title: Pin headers
headers.text: 30 pins in the Arduino Nano layout: 3V3, 5V, GND and the GPIO you wire screens, readers and mics to.
